sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Office Acceptance Debate**: The conflict between 'Pro-changers' (Rajagopalachari, Patel, Prasad) who favored office acceptance to provide relief and 'Anti-changers' (Nehru, Subhash Bose, Socialists) who feared it would lead to constitutionalism and compromise.
• **The Compromise**: Congress decided to contest elections to 'combat' the 1935 Act from within, but accepted office only after Lord Linlithgow provided assurances that Governors would not use 'special powers' to interfere in day-to-day administration.
• **Electoral Performance**: Congress won absolute majorities in 5 provinces (Madras, UP, CP, Bihar, Orissa) and emerged as the largest party in 3 others (Bombay, Assam, NWFP).
• **Key Metric**: The ministries lasted for 28 months, resigning in October 1939 due to the unilateral inclusion of India in WWII without consulting the Indian people.

A report published by the Muslim League in 1938 alleging that Congress ministries were biased against Muslims; used to justify the 'Deliverance Day' in 1939.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Civil Liberties**: Lifting bans on newspapers, political organizations, and returning confiscated arms licenses.
• **Labor Relations**: Appointment of committees to improve working conditions, though the Congress often mediated between labor and capital to avoid strikes.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Internal Friction**: Tension between the parliamentary wing and the organizational wing (Congress High Command).
• **Communal Polarization**: The rise of the Muslim League's 'Congress Tyranny' narrative, which deepened the communal divide.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'B-O-M-P-U-C-I-N' (The 8 Provinces: Bombay, Orissa, Madras, Punjab-No, UP, CP, India-No, NWFP, Bihar).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Remember the 8 provinces where Congress formed ministries: Madras, UP, CP, Bihar, Orissa, Bombay, NWFP, and Assam (later).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often asks if Congress formed ministries in Punjab or Bengal. They did NOT. Punjab had the Unionist Party, and Bengal had the Krishak Praja Party-Muslim League coalition.
Mains Value Addition: Use the phrase 'The 28-month experiment' to describe the period, highlighting that it was a 'training ground' for future Indian administrators.

keyTakeaways: Congress ministries proved that Indians were capable of self-governance, debunking the 'White Man's Burden' myth.
The period highlighted the limitations of the 1935 Act, specifically the Governor's veto power.
The resignation in 1939 marked the end of constitutional agitation and the beginning of the final phase of the freedom struggle.
